correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the triangular graph has diameter at most two; an induced three-vertex path is exactly a forbidden geodesic triple. Equivalently, the selected edges of K_n contain no four-vertex path as a subgraph. Their connected components are vertex-disjoint stars, triangles and isolates. The all-set labeled block weights are 1,z,3z²+z³ and kz^(k−1) for k≥4. A two-edge star can be completed to a triangle; any isolate can extend a star, and two isolates can be joined. Conversely, an edge joining distinct non-isolated components retains two disjoint edges in a single component, an edge from a lone isolate into a triangle is likewise forbidden, and an internal added edge in a star on ≥4 vertices destroys the component type. Thus the maximal spanning blocks are edges, triangles and stars on ≥4 vertices; the only nonspanning type is triangles and one isolate. The labeled SET formula gives both EGFs as printed, including A_0=M_0=A_1=M_1=1. For n even the excess over n/2 vanishes only for pure pairs. For odd spanning n, an odd block is required; the minimum excess 3/2 occurs only for one triangle or one five-vertex star, with all other blocks pairs. The one-isolate case has n−1 selected edges and, for odd n≥5, is feasible only at n≥7, so cannot tie. These types give the displayed factorials; n=3 has only the full triangle, and z^n requires all triangle blocks. Complementation gives inclusion-minimal cluster deletion sets (the displayed z counts retained vertices, not deletions).
residual_risks: The graph statement includes n=2 directly; n=0,1 are EGF conventions. Recorded finite checks were not treated as proofs or independently replayed.

evidence: The general structural theorem gives induced clique components. On line graphs of cliques, Ghorbani et al. use clique components on disjoint supports and compute the GP maximum. Di Stefano et al. use the disjoint triangle/star forms with one or at least three edges per star in the maximal case and derive the minimum possible maximal size.
The general-position polynomial paper defines the all-set size polynomial, but the inspected definition and examples do not give these evaluated EGFs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier component descriptions, not just the cardinality optima or the name of the polynomial, are the dominating input. The only needed treatment not expressed by the types alone is the trivial comparison of isolated vertices with available star centers.

evidence: For components of size k≥3 the k star-center choices and the one triangle on k=3 exhaust the old clique description; the two-vertex star has one choice. Exponentiating the block series counts disjoint labeled components, with no unsolved interaction.

The earlier maximal forms have no three-vertex star. The isolated-vertex test produces only the extra t exp(z³t³/6) term. A least-size odd spanning configuration uses a triangle or five-vertex star with pairs, giving exactly the stated elementary multinomial counts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The evaluated statements were not found printed in the inspected earlier proofs, but their content is already determined by applying standard labeled SET counting directly to the earlier forms. This is stronger coverage than knowing only the extremal degrees.

originality.rationale: The content is an explicit enumerative restatement of known component structure. For all sets, the prior clique-union characterization and its prior application to L(K_n) now require only the star-center weights and the labeled SET formula. For maximal sets, the earlier triangle/star structure leaves a single immediate isolate test: a spare vertex extends a star, and two spare vertices accommodate an edge. This gives precisely the stated extra EGF summand and all minimum-degree counts by choosing the unique odd block, if any, and pairing the rest. The two exact matching catalogue formulas were also inspected; their later path dates do not establish priority and are not the basis for attributing earlier discovery. The substantive originality requirement fails because the assigned formulas and multiplicities are mechanical consequences of the earlier structure, not because the dates of the matching formulas prove prior publication.
residual_risks: Neither catalogue overlap establishes provenance or priority for the evaluated formulas. Literal keyword misses in the polynomial paper were not interpreted as covering the full source. No claim is made about whether the exact formulas were printed before the frozen item.

value.rationale: The polynomial and the graph family are motivated. Here the coefficients are obtained from the known labeled component decomposition by the textbook SET formula, and the boundary multiplicities are the direct multinomial counts for those same blocks. The presentation is convenient but supplies no independently needed exact fact not mechanically provided by that structure.
residual_risks: This does not assess polynomials for other families, where the maximal component structure may require genuinely new work.
